references.text: The original instruction for the ephod to be made of gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
The description of the belt on the ephod, which was to be made of the same materials, including gold and the colored yarns.
The instruction for the breastpiece to be crafted with skillful work from gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
The description of the craftsmen's skills in performing skilled work with blue, purple, and scarlet wool and fine linen.
The curtain for the tabernacle was made of blue, purple, and scarlet wool and finely twisted linen with skillful work.
The direct context where the ephod was made of gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
The belt on the ephod was made from the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
The breastpiece was crafted with skillful work using the same materials mentioned in verse 3.
The command regarding materials in the instructions (Exodus 28:5) is directly fulfilled in the execution of the work (Exodus 39:3).
Both verses document the skilled craftsmanship of various parts of the high priest's garments within the same account.
